title: Proper morphisms: compact supports equal direct image
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\ f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\ Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y\end{array}$$
be a cartesian square of schemes with $f$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], regarded as a compact-support square [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Work throughout in $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $c_0=(\operatorname{id}_X,f)$ be the identity compactification [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], and identify its base change with $c'_0=(\operatorname{id}_{X'},f')$ by the canonical pullback identification. Let $a_T:(\operatorname{id}_T)_!\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$ be the canonical identification furnished by the sheafification description of extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], applied degreewise. Define
$$\alpha_{f,K}=Rf_*(a_{X,K}):Rf_!^{c_0}K=Rf_*(\operatorname{id}_X)_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K,$$
and define $\alpha_{f',L}$ in the same way.

The same identity-open normalization is used for the finite-level pro-etale compact-support direct image. Suppose moreover that $X,Y$ are finite-type schemes over a field $K_0$ in which a prime $\ell$ is invertible, fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $n\geq1$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$, as in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Let $a^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T}:(\operatorname{id}_T)_!\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$ be the canonical identification furnished by the sheafification description of pro-etale extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero], applied degreewise, and define
$$\alpha^{\mathrm{proet}}_{f,M}=Rf_{*,n}(a^{\mathrm{proet}}_{X,M}):Rf_{!,n}^{c_0}M=Rf_{*,n}(\operatorname{id}_X)_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,n}M,\qquad M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n}),$$
with $Rf_{!,n}^{c_0}$ the functor of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] at the identity compactification and $Rf_{*,n}$ the derived direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. This natural isomorphism is the canonical proper identification $Rf_{!,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,n}$ at the identity compactification.

For every $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, the compact-support exchange of [def-cbc-exchange-map] satisfies
$$\alpha_{f',g'^{-1}K}\circ\operatorname{Ex}^{c_0}_!(K)
=\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{*,\square}(K)\circ g^{-1}(\alpha_{f,K}),$$
where $\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{*,\square}$ is the module-coefficient mate of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], as specified in [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. These are the exchange transformations typed in [sk-def-sf-exchanges], here for the specified finite-ring etale operations. The equality is natural in $K$. It also describes the compactification-independent exchange of [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] after its canonical comparisons with $c_0,c'_0$. Consequently the isomorphism asserted there specializes, for proper $f$, to the isomorphism for this specified proper-base-change exchange. No additional hypothesis on $g$, constructibility, residue characteristics, or quasi-compactness of the schemes is imposed.

proof.text: Use the identity compactification of [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]; its base change is the identity-open compactification of $f'$ under the canonical pullback identification, as in [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. For $j=\operatorname{id}_T$, every etale object $V\to T$ factors uniquely through $j$. Thus the presheaf defining $j_!F$ in [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] is exactly $F$, with the same restrictions. Since $F$ is already a sheaf its sheafification identifies canonically with $F$; this is $a_{T,F}$. The explicit counit in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] is the identity on every $F(V)$, so this identification is precisely the identity-open adjunction normalization, not an arbitrary automorphism of the identity functor. Its unit is the inverse identification by the triangle identity. Applying the identification degreewise gives $a_T$ on complexes and in $D^+$, and applying $Rf_*$ gives the isomorphism $\alpha_f$ in the statement.

proof.text: The pro-etale identification of the statement is defined exactly as in step 1. For $j=\operatorname{id}_T$ every object $V\to T$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ factors uniquely through $j$, so the module presheaf $P_M$ of [def-weil-extension-by-zero] is $M$ itself, with the same restrictions and the same $A$-action. Since $M$ is already a sheaf of $A$-modules, the sheafification map $M=P_M\to P_M^\#$ of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] is an $A$-linear isomorphism; its inverse is $a^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,M}:(\operatorname{id}_T)_!M\to M$. It is natural in $M$ because $(\operatorname{id}_T)_!\alpha$ is the sheafification of $P_\alpha=\alpha$. Thus $(\operatorname{id}_T)_!$ is naturally isomorphic to the identity functor; it is exact and acts degreewise [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], so the degreewise isomorphism of complexes preserves quasi-isomorphisms and descends to $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$. For the identity compactification $c_0=(\operatorname{id}_X,f)$ the functor of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] is $Rf_{*,n}(\operatorname{id}_X)_!$, so applying $Rf_{*,n}$ to $a^{\mathrm{proet}}_X$ gives the natural isomorphism $\alpha^{\mathrm{proet}}_f$ of the statement. No exchange property is asserted on the pro-etale side.

proof.text:
In the upper open square both vertical open immersions are identities. Write $I_T=(\operatorname{id}_T)_!$, $H=g'^{-1}$, and let $\beta_K:HI_XK\to I_{X'}HK$ be the degreewise map of [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]. Its inverse is, by [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change], the adjoint transpose of the unit followed by the inverse-image square identification. Under $a_X:I_X\cong\operatorname{id}$ and $a_{X'}:I_{X'}\cong\operatorname{id}$ the two units are identities, by the explicit adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and step 1. The square identification is also the identity after the canonical identity-inverse-image identifications: both paths are restriction along $g'$. Hence that transpose is the identity of $HK$, and its inverse is the identity as well. In the original notation this says exactly
$$a_{X',HK}\circ\beta_K=H(a_{X,K}).$$
This is a calculation with the specified mate, not merely the existence of a base-change isomorphism. It holds degreewise and hence on the derived categories.

proof.text:
Put $E_M=\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{*,\square}(M)$. The coefficient version is the same mate as [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], by [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. In particular it is a natural transformation in $M$. Formula [def-cbc-exchange-map] for $c_0$ reads
$$\operatorname{Ex}^{c_0}_!(K)=Rf'_*(\beta_K)\circ E_{I_XK}.$$
Compose with $\alpha_{f',HK}=Rf'_*(a_{X',HK})$. Step 3 and functoriality, followed by naturality of $E$ for $a_{X,K}:I_XK\to K$, give the explicit equality
$$\begin{aligned}
\alpha_{f',HK}\circ\operatorname{Ex}^{c_0}_!(K)
&=Rf'_*(a_{X',HK}\circ\beta_K)\circ E_{I_XK}\\
&=Rf'_*(H(a_{X,K}))\circ E_{I_XK}\\
&=E_K\circ g^{-1}(Rf_*(a_{X,K}))
=E_K\circ g^{-1}(\alpha_{f,K}).
\end{aligned}$$
Every equality is an equality of the displayed arrows, and the constructions are natural in $K$. This proves the required coincidence with the specified proper exchange.

proof.text: Apply [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] to $c_0$. Its hypotheses are precisely a finite commutative ring, a separated finite-type map with a supplied compactification, an arbitrary base change, and a bounded-below complex. Proper $f$ is separated and finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $c_0$ supplies the compactification, so all these hypotheses hold. The theorem makes $\operatorname{Ex}^{c_0}_!(K)$ invertible. Both $\alpha$ maps and their inverse-image images are isomorphisms, so the equality of step 4 makes $E_K$ invertible. The same theorem says its exchange maps agree under canonical compactification comparisons, independently of the common refinement. Therefore its compactification-independent map becomes the map computed in step 4 when the functors are identified using $c_0,c'_0$. This also proves the asserted specialization for any initial compactification. No compactification-independence lemma with an extra qcqs hypothesis is needed.
